# Public artifact preparation

Prepare clear, source-backed material for Evident Technologies LLC. Read repository governance and inspect the current branch, worktree, and diff before editing. Preserve existing work, source provenance, security policy, and runner boundaries.

## Scope and authority

Use the approved task scope. Public documentation describes implemented behavior and explicitly qualified development work. Do not invent availability, certification, trademark clearance, ownership, or founder approval. Review policy changes as proposals; documentation cannot grant access or production authority.

## Public artifact sequence

Inspect, classify, sanitize, fingerprint, and review before any separately authorized publication. For public Gists, publication requires manual human approval. Never mass-publish raw repository excerpts.

Reject secrets, credentials, cookies, private endpoints, provider identifiers, internal topology, private repository references, privileged orchestration, personal records, litigation material, client information, and unreviewed speculative fragments. Detailed rejection and exposure findings stay private.

## Provenance and handoff

For a curated artifact, record its source revision, canonical filename, SHA-256, UTC preparation time, authorship or source attribution, rights, classification, and approval status. A hash identifies bytes; it does not establish authenticity, ownership, or approval. Preserve upstream licenses and distinguish original work from derivatives.

Public examples should be small, self-contained, synthetic, and useful. Explain dependencies and limitations. Do not include private authorship metadata or sensitive location information. The published artifact must identify the company accurately without treating historical account handles as current authority.

Use the existing owner for repository review, lane management, CI admission, and deployment. A local check, draft PR, or approved publication candidate does not authorize merge, deployment, provider changes, or disclosure of private material.
